questions.question:
Which of the following is/are a capital receipt for the government ?

(A) Loans taken by the government from the public

(B) Borrowings from foreign countries and Institutes

(C) Disinvestment of assets
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All - A, B and C.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Capital receipts** refer to the **inflow of funds** that create liabilities or reduce assets for the government.
 
• Loans taken by the government from the public, borrowings from **foreign countries and institutes**, and disinvestment of assets are all examples of capital receipts.
 
• Loans taken by the government from the public are a form of** borrowing **and **create a liability** for the government.
 
• **Borrowings **from foreign countries and institutes also create a liability for the government and are usually accompanied by conditions and terms of repayment.
 
• **Disinvestment of assets **refers to the sale of government-owned assets like **shares, land, or buildings, and generates revenue** for the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capital receipts** are earnings from **non-routine or infrequently** occurring activity.
 
• An organization's primary or consistent source of income is **not** capital receipts.
 
• Additionally, due to their capital nature, these receipts are displayed on a **company's balance sheet **rather than in the income statement or profit and loss account.
 
• The recording of these receipts follows the** accrual method.**
 
• Additionally, unlike revenue receipts, capital receipts cannot be used for the distribution of profit due to their **non-recurring nature**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a variable cost for a firm ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Property taxes.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Variable costs **are expenses that** vary** with the level of production or sales.

 
 
• They increase as production or sales** increase and decrease** as production or sales decrease.
 
 
 
• In contrast, **fixed costs** are expenses that** do not vary** with production or sales levels.
 
• **Commissions and labor costs** are both examples of** variable costs.**
 
 
• Commissions are paid based on the **level of sales**, so they increase when sales increase and decrease when sales decrease.
 
• Labor costs similarly **increase **as production increases and **decrease **as production decreases.
 
 
 
• **Packing costs** could be either a** variable or fixed cost** depending on how they are structured.
 
 
• If the cost of packing materials and labor varies with the level of production, then it is a** variable cost**.
 
• If it is a** fixed cost** that does not vary with production levels, then it is a fixed cost.
 
 
 
• **Property taxes**, on the other hand, are typically a **fixed cost**.
 
 
• They are based on the assessed value of the property and** do not vary** with production or sales levels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Commissions** are **payments** made to salespeople or other employees based on their level of sales or performance.

 
 
• They are a form of** incentive compensation** that is designed to** motivate employees **to work harder and sell more.
 
 
 
• **Property taxes** are taxes that are levied on **real estate property**.
 
 
• They are typically assessed by local governments and are based on the** value** of the property.
 
• They are used to fund a variety of** local services**, such as schools, police, and fire departments.
 
 
 
• **Labor costs **are the wages and benefits paid to employees.
 
 
• They are a **major expense** for many companies and can vary widely depending on the type of work being done and the location of the company.
 
 
 
• **Packing costs** are the expenses associated with packaging and shipping products.
 
 
• They can include the **cost of materials, labor, and shipping fees.**

__
 
• **Original Jurisdiction** refers to the power of a court to hear a case for the** first time,** instead of on appeal or by review of another court's decision.
 
• In the **United States**, the Supreme Court has **original jurisdiction** in a limited number of cases, such as disputes between states or cases involving ambassadors or other public ministers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Appellate Jurisdiction** refers to the power of a court to **review and revise** the decisions of a** lower court.**

 
 
• The Supreme Court has appellate jurisdiction over most cases, and it is the** highest court of appeal** in the United States.
 
 
 
• **Advisory Jurisdiction** refers to the power of a court to provide **legal advice **or opinions, rather than to decide specific cases.
 
 
• The Supreme Court** does not** have advisory jurisdiction in the United States.
 
 
 
• **Writ Jurisdiction** refers to the power of a court to** issue writs, or orders**, to government officials or agencies.
 
 
• The Supreme Court has **writ jurisdiction**, and it can issue writs such as** habeas corpus, mandamus, and certiorari.**

questions.question: Identify the FALSE statement regarding circulation of blood in fishes.

options.text: Blood from the ventricle goes only to the gills.
Blood is sent from the gills to the rest of the body.
Blood from the body enters the auricle .
The two chambered heart provides double circulation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Two chambered heart

 
 
• ​The heart of some animals, like fish, only has two chambers. There is only one ventricle and one auricle in their heart.
 
• The sinus venosus, which leads to the atrium, and the bulbus arteriosus, which follows the ventricle, are on their flanks.
 
• The sinus venosus is where the deoxygenated blood enters the atrium. It enters the ventricle from here.
 
• When the blood is pumped out of the ventricle, the pressure is much higher than that at the gills, which are the next place the blood goes.
 
• Because of their thin walls, the gills run the risk of being damaged by high blood pressure. As a result, the blood pressure that comes out of the ventricle is adjusted by the bulbus arteriosus.
 
• The blood's pressure must still be sufficient to circulate the fluid throughout the body, even though the decreased pressure may prevent damage to the lungs.
 
• As a result, a fish's blood circulation relies on a delicate balance between low pressure for the gills and sufficient circulation. Fishes do not have double circulation, unlike humans.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Three chambered heart

 
 
• ​With the exception of crocodiles, the hearts of all reptiles have three chambers, with two auricles and one ventricle. Compared to fish, this type is more advanced, but not as advanced as mammals.
 
• However, the ventricle is divided into two sub chambers by an incomplete partition. The right ventricle, also known as the Calum pulmonale, and the left ventricle, also known as the Calum venosum, are the two sub chambers.
 
• A third sub chamber, the cavum arteriosum, is located toward the top of the ventricle. A valve connects it to the left ventricle.
 
• Blood that has lost oxygen makes its way into the right atrium and into the right sub chamber of the ventricle. However, it also leaks into and fills the left ventricle as a result of incomplete separation.
 
• After that, the blood ascends the ventricle and enters the lungs for oxygenation. This descends once more and clogs the third chamber, the cavum arteriosum, temporarily.
 
• After that, the blood flows into the left ventricle, where it reaches the rest of the body.

questions.question:
Consider the magnitudes and directions of the induced potential difference in the following situations:

(a) A magnet moving with a speed of 1 m/s with its north pole towards a stationary coil.

(b) The same magnet moving with a speed of 1 m/s with its south pole towards the same stationary coil.

The induced potential differences are of ______ magnitude(s) and have ______ sign(s) in the above two cases
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**same, opposite.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In both cases, the induced potential differences are of the **same magnitude.**
 
• In case (a), the induced potential difference has the **same sign** as that of the magnet's north pole, i.e., it is positive.
 
• In case (b), the induced potential difference has the **opposite sign** as that of the magnet's south pole, i.e., it is negative.
 
• The magnitude of the induced potential difference depends on the **rate of change of magnetic flux **through the coil, which, in turn, depends on the **speed and orientation** of the magnet.
 
• The induced potential difference is given by the formula: **V = -N du/dt, **where V is the induced potential difference, N is the number of turns in the coil, and du/dt is the rate of change of magnetic flux through the coil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Induced potential difference** refers to the **voltage generated** in a conductor when it is subjected to a **changing magnetic field**.
 
• An **electric potential difference** is created in the coil by the pace at which the** number of magnetic field lines** connected to the loop changes while the magnet and loop are **moving relative** to one another or by a** change in current **in a nearby conductor.
 
• The circuit resistance is** inversely proportional** to the induced current, and it is** proportional** to the induced electromotive force.
 
• Although there is** no current **when the circuit is open, there may be an **induced electromotive force.**

questions.question: During the preparation of NaOH by chlor-alkali process, which of the following ions migrates toward the cathode ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Na+**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chlor-alkali process is a method used for the production of NaOH, Cl2, and H2 gas.
 
• In this process, NaCl is electrolyzed in a diaphragm cell with the help of a direct current.
 
• The diaphragm cell consists of an anode, a cathode, and a diaphragm that separates the anode and cathode compartments.
 
• At the anode, Cl- ion is oxidized to form Cl2 gas, and at the cathode, H+ ions are reduced to form H2 gas.
 
• During the electrolysis, Na+ and OH- ions are formed at the cathode compartment due to the migration of Na+ ion towards the anode and OH- ion towards the cathode.
 
• The OH- ion reacts with the H+ ion to form water, and the Na+ ion reacts with the Cl- ion to form NaCl.
 
• The NaCl is then separated from the NaOH solution, and the NaOH solution is further purified to obtain solid NaOH.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Na+ ion **does not migrate towards the cathode during the chlor-alkali process. It migrates towards the anode.
 
• **Cl- ion** migrates towards the anode during the chlor-alkali process. It is oxidized to form Cl2 gas.
 
• **OH- ion** migrates towards the cathode during the preparation of NaOH by chlor-alkali process.
 
• **CO32- ion** is not involved in the chlor-alkali process. It is a carbonate ion that is present in some minerals and rocks.
